A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pairmixer research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training experiments, RCSB/CASP15 evaluations, inference and binder-design runtimes, architectural ablations, and Match3 results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds biomolecular benchmark evaluations, component ablations, locality tests, distogram evaluations, and recycling analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same incoming/outgoing triangle multiplication and feed-forward updates. The treatment of sequence representations, MSA module, diffusion module, and BindFast integration is unchanged. The new local-dropout intervention is an analysis of the existing model, not a revised proposed architecture.

E1.justification: V2 Table 1 and Appendix C.3 add evaluations on 298 PoseBusters protein–ligand complexes, 70 antibody–antigen complexes, 172 protein–nucleic-acid complexes, and 27 RNA-only structures. These substantially broaden the explicitly evaluated populations and structural tasks beyond v1's reported coverage. RCSB, CASP15, binder design, and Match3 remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain AlphaFold3, Chai-1, Boltz-1/Pairformer, and the sequence-only Transformer; Match3 retains its second- and third-order attention comparators. The added evaluations reuse existing comparison methods. The new module-removal variants serve as Pairformer ablation controls.

E3.justification: V2 introduces substantial protocols for new experiments: date filtering and deduplication for PoseBusters, longer Pairmixer fine-tuning for that comparison, matched-iteration modality evaluations using ICS/IPS, and 12-layer Pairformer ablations trained for 60 epochs on 3M samples. Locality masking, direct distogram/contact metrics, and accuracy evaluation at 0, 1, 3, and 10 recycles add further procedures. The original main training and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of local versus long-range interactions (Figure 9), individual Pairformer component removal (Table 6), performance stratified by sequence length and MSA depth (Figure 16), backbone quality independent of diffusion decoding (Table 8), and recycling sensitivity (Table 9). The original mixing/dimension ablations, Match3 experiment, and head-to-head comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals for the system-level RCSB/CASP15 comparisons, and the Match3 error-bar figure is unchanged. V2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: RCSB/CASP15 Tables 4–5 are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results. Table 1 reports PoseBusters RMSD<2 of 0.67 for Pairmixer versus 0.68 for Boltz-1, antibody DockQ success of 0.23 for both versus 0.08 for Transformer, and RNA lDDT of 0.59, 0.58, and 0.61 respectively. New diagnostic outcomes appear in Tables 6, 8–9 and Figures 9 and 16. The binder-runtime table also corrects reversed method assignments in the first five rows; its speedup claims are retained.

T1.justification: Section 6 adds the formal local-interaction mask M(z_ik)=1 when |i-k|≤B and zero otherwise. This is a limited mathematical definition supporting the new diagnostic. Existing architectural equations, Match3 definitions, and FLOPs derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly extends the parity claim to antibody–antigen, protein–nucleic-acid, and RNA structures, and describes sparse long-range interactions. It also narrows the binder sequence-length claim from beyond 800 to beyond 700 amino acids. The central attention-free architecture contribution and headline training/inference efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 develops the mechanism interpretation from sparse interactions to sparse long-range interactions. Appendices D.1 and D.4–D.6 add a short-training qualification and arguments against performance parity arising only from favorable inputs, diffusion correction, or recycling. Section 5.5 also proposes limited RNA training data as an explanation for the Transformer's RNA advantage; this remains a hypothesis.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, plus preparation details for the added benchmarks and disclosure of the 64-bin distogram head. The extensive optimizer, hardware, crop-size, architecture, and FLOPs information is retained in renumbered Table 10. The precise additional PoseBusters fine-tuning budget is not specified.

R1.justification: V2 adds Moult et al. (2014) to support contact-prediction evaluation. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier structure predictors and attention-free architectures otherwise remain unchanged; relocated binder-design citations are retained.

P1.justification: Targeted editing condenses the main binder-design discussion, moves its detailed treatment to Appendix C.4, and consolidates Match3 discussion in D.3. Appendix material is regrouped into additional results and additional analyses. Most introductory, methodological, related-work, and concluding prose remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the displays with the four-part benchmark Table 1, new ablation/distogram/recycling Tables 6, 8, and 9, and locality and stratification Figures 9 and 16. Existing displays are retained but several are relocated or renumbered. The binder-runtime table's method headings and corresponding entries are corrected.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for generality and backbone sufficiency. Dedicated biomolecular evaluations address v1's limited modality-specific validation, while direct distogram, component-removal, locality, and recycling tests probe important alternative explanations for its results. Runtime-label and sequence-length corrections also improve accuracy. The extra PoseBusters fine-tuning budget remains underspecified and the RNA explanation is speculative, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger support for the paper's central conclusions.
